2. The present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 18 of 2004. The plaintiff-petitioners case is that they are the heirs of Sreemati Shantimoyee Chowdhury and on her death they have inherited the property. The further case of the petitioners are that the opposite party No.1 instituted a partition suit being Other Suit No. 32 of 1986 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong for partition of the suit property against said Shantimoyee Chowdhury. It is contended by the petitioner that during pendency of the aforesaid suit i.e. Other Suit No. 32 of 1986, Shantimoyee Chowdhury died but her heirs were not substituted in the said suit and without doing that the opposite party No. 1 obtained the ex parte decree in the aforesaid suit behind the back of the heirs of said Shantimoyee Chowdhury. After obtaining the decree the opposite party No.1 also started Execution Case No. 5 of 2003 before the executing Court and during the pendency of the aforesaid Execution Case the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 18 of 2004 against the opposite parties for a declaration that the decree obtained in other suit No. 32 of 1986 is fraudulent, collusive, inoperative and, as such, not binding upon the plaintiffs. After filing of the aforesaid suit the present petitioners filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, hereinafter called "the Code", praying for an injunction to restrain the opposite party No.1 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property and also to stay all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 5 of 2003 pending before the Court of learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong. The trial Court by its order dated 10-2-2004 issued a show cause notice and ad interim order of status quo was granted till 16-3-2004 but as the opposite party No. 1 i.e. the plaintiff of Other Suit No. 32 of 1986, did not file any written objection, the trial Court by its order dated 23-5-2004 confirmed the order of status quo and also stayed all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 5 of 2003 till the disposal of Other Suit No. 18 of 2004. 

 "(1) save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Joint District Judge shall lie— 

 (a) to the District Judge where the value of the Original Suit in which or in any proceeding arising out of which the decree or order was made did not exceed five lac Taka. 

 (2) Save as aforesaid, an appeal from a decree or order of a Senior Assistant Judge or an Assistant Judge shall lie to the District Judge. 

 12. We have earlier quoted the provision of section 115(2) of the Code, a reading of which shows that there is nothing in the sub-section expressly providing that a revision will lie against an order of a Joint District Judge before the District Judge irrespective of the value of the subject-matter of the suit or proceeding pending in the Court of Joint District Judge where ordinarily suits and proceedings of unlimited valuation are filed. There is no doubt that an appeal against a decree or an order of Joint District Judge can be filed before the District Judge only when the value of the subject matter of the suit or proceeding is up to Taka 5,00,000. If that be so no revision can be preferred before a District Judge where the value of the subject-matter of suit or proceeding is above Taka 5,00,000 as it is beyond the pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Judge. Always revisional forum has been determined with reference to the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Appellate Court. Thus, it is apparent that the intention of the legislature was that the pecuniary jurisdiction of the revisional Court as usual will be determined by the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Court in the matter of appeal. In the absence of any express provision in the new sub-section (2) of section 115 of the Code it must be presumed that the legislature intended that the revisional forum will be as before determined by the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Appellate Court. Thus, the District Judge can exercise his power of revision under section 115(2) of the Code where his pecuniary jurisdiction in revisional matter is co-extensive with that of his appellate jurisdiction, i.e. where the value of the subject-matter does not exceed the appellate jurisdiction. Therefore, in the instant case the District Judge lacked inherent jurisdiction to entertain the revisional application against the order of learned Joint District Judge as the valuation of the suit is over five lac. Besides, in this Court the valuation of the revisional application is always fixed at the valuation of the suit i.e. in this Division the revision is controlled by the Appellate Side Rules namely, part I, Chapter II, Rule 1, and Schedules thereto. Clause (3) of the Schedule provides for applications for revision under section 115 of the Code against Orders of Subordinate Judiciary.
